coverage: Roster: every source the angle names was pursued. FETCHED AND SUBSTANTIVE (18): Extrapolation (Gerlach 1999), Foundation (Jones 1989), Science Fiction Studies #46 (McCaffery interview 1988, via Wayback), First Things (Farrell 2007), Aramini's UNLV dissertation (2019), the Hall interview chapter from Peter Wright's Shadows of the New Sun (Liverpool UP 2007), eight Ultan's Library papers including Peter Wright's Birmingham conference paper and Wowra's toponymy study, two John Clute review-essays, the Nova Express interview, and Wikipedia as a declared relay. FETCHED BUT NOT USABLE (5): Joan Gordon's 1986 Starmont monograph (41MB scan, OCR interleaves the two columns so no sentence verifies verbatim), Clareson's 1985 SFRA column (Wolfe only in passing), gwern's 2005-green (image-only scan), and two further Ultan pieces (thematic or superseded). BLOCKED (6): the SFS reviews of Attending Daedalus (2005) and of Gordon (1987) — depauw.edu 404s site-wide with no Wayback capture of the review pages and the DOIs are not open access; Logos 2015 "Art and Allegory"; Critical Quarterly 2020; Cambridge Core's Shadows introduction (zero bytes returned); and UNLV's own copy of the dissertation (403, read via the gwern mirror instead). Peter Wright's monograph Attending Daedalus itself was reached only through Aramini's and Wright's own quotations of it, and those three claims are marked medium confidence. Substantive sources per route: gwern.net scholarly PDF directory 5, Ultan's Library 8, Wayback 1, live web 3, relay 1; discovery by named roster, then gwern's Gene Wolfe document directory, then OpenAlex bibliography chasing (273 hits), then the Ultan article index. THIN-LITERATURE FINDING: no stylometric or corpus study of Wolfe's prose appears to exist — a targeted search returned only generic stylometry methodology with no Wolfe content — and two scholars in this corpus say the same thing independently (Clute 2009: "academics have notoriously tended to shun him for decades"; Wright 2002: Searles's prophecy of an academic field day "has gone largely unfulfilled"). The web-search budget for this session was exhausted at the end of the sweep; the last two searches surfaced nothing new.
